```plato
    // The body with its velocity advanced by a wrench and gravity, then damped —
    // the FIRST half of a semi-implicit step. Gravity is an acceleration, so it is
    // added directly rather than through the inverse mass, and it is scaled by the
    // body's own multiplier; an immovable body has no inverse mass and so feels
    // neither the wrench nor, through the same zero, its own weight.
    //
    // The GYROSCOPIC term is omitted. Euler's equation has an extra
    // -I^-1 (omega x I omega) on the angular update, and it is what makes a
    // tumbling body with three different moments flip end over end. Integrated
    // EXPLICITLY, as it would have to be here, that term adds energy at every step
    // and a fast-spinning body diverges — which is why engines that want it solve
    // it implicitly, as its own small non-linear system. Omitting it is exact for
    // any body with two equal moments (every ball, cylinder and capsule here) and
    // costs a box its tumbling instability.
    IntegrateVelocity(self: SolverBody3D, wrench: SpatialForce3D, gravity: Vector3D,
        seconds: Number): SolverBody3D
    {
        var accelerating = self.InverseMass > 0.0;
        var linear = self.Velocity.Linear
            + (wrench.Force * self.InverseMass
                + (accelerating ? gravity * self.GravityScale : Vector3D.Zero)) * seconds;
        var angular = self.Velocity.Angular + AngularResponse(self, wrench.Torque * seconds);
        return WithVelocity(self, SpatialVelocity3D(
            linear * DampingFactor(self.LinearDamping, seconds),
            angular * DampingFactor(self.AngularDamping, seconds)));
    }
```
